subject: Genetics
title: The Identical Genome Myth
description: A 60-second lesson on The Identical Genome Myth.

hook.text: The first genome was called 'the human genome.' But whose genome was it? Not yours. Not exactly anyone's.

buildup.text: The reference genome was assembled from multiple anonymous donors. It's a mosaic—no single person's actual DNA.

discovery.text: Later analysis found most of the reference came from one man: a Buffalo, New York donor known only as RP11.

twist.text: A white American male's DNA became 'the' human reference. Billions of humans weren't represented. Bias was built in.

climax.text: The pangenome project now includes diverse populations. A single reference can never capture human variation.

punchline.text: The 'human genome' was one man's. The real one is everyone's.

quiz.question: What is a key problem with the original reference genome?
